answer: Resist sybils with TPM-bound identity cards: each agent proves it runs on one real, tamper-proof chip. First, the device's TPM signs a unique attestation key that cannot be cloned. Second, the network issues one identity per attestation and rejects any second claim from the same chip. Third, a flagged chip is blacklisted forever, so the hardware turns worthless for fraud. Forging 10,000 identities means buying 10,000 TPM chips at $40 each, $400,000 plus 10,000 machines to run them. A hollow promise meets a canyon wall, and trust feels like velvet only after the chip proves itself real.
